facts.text: You must have proof of financial responsibility (insurance) with you when you drive and for a drive test.

cites.quote: You must have your proof of financial responsibility (insurance) when you drive and for a drive test.

facts.text: If you are in a collision, you must show proof of insurance to the other drivers involved.

cites.quote: If you get into a collision, you must show proof to the other drivers involved in the collision.

facts.text: Your insurance must cover at least $30,000 for a single death or injury.

cites.quote: Your insurance must cover at least:
$30,000 for a single death or injury.

facts.text: Your insurance must cover at least $60,000 for death or injury to more than one person.

cites.quote: Your insurance must cover at least:
$60,000 for death or injury to more than one person.

facts.text: Your insurance must cover at least $15,000 for property damage.

cites.quote: Your insurance must cover at least:
$15,000 for property damage.

facts.text: Parents or guardians take on financial responsibility for drivers under 18 and pay for damages if the driver is in a collision; drivers 18 and older are responsible for themselves.

cites.quote: Parents or guardians take on financial responsibility for drivers younger than 18 years old and pay for damages if the driver is involved in a collision. Drivers who are 18 years old and older take on their own financial responsibility.

facts.text: Before buying insurance, make sure the agent, broker, or provider is licensed by the California Department of Insurance.

cites.quote: Before you buy insurance, make sure that the agent, broker, or insurance provider is licensed by the California Department of Insurance.

facts.text: If you are in a collision without proper insurance, your driving privilege will be suspended for up to four years, no matter who was at fault.

cites.quote: Your driving privilege will be suspended for up to four years if you are in a collision and do not have proper insurance coverage. It does not matter who was at fault.

facts.text: After an uninsured-collision suspension, you can get your license back during the last three years if you provide and maintain an SR 22/SR 1P insurance certificate for that three-year period.

cites.quote: You can get your driver’s license back during the last three years of the suspension if you provide a California Insurance Proof Certificate (SR 22/SR 1P) and maintain it during the three-year period.

facts.text: If you cannot afford liability insurance, you may be eligible for the California Low Cost Automobile Insurance Program.

cites.quote: If you cannot afford liability insurance, you may be eligible for the California Low Cost Automobile Insurance Program.

facts.text: The most common causes of collisions are driver distractions, unsafe speed, improper turns, not following right-of-way rules, not obeying stop signals and signs, driving on the wrong side of the road, and traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

cites.quote: The most common causes of collisions are:
Driver distractions.
Unsafe speed.
Improper turns.
Not following the right-of-way rules.
Not following stop signals and signs.
Driving on the wrong side of the road.
A vehicle traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

facts.text: If you see a vehicle's emergency flashers ahead, slow down and pass carefully; there may be a collision or other emergency.

cites.quote: If you see a vehicle’s emergency flashers ahead, slow down. There may be a collision or other road emergency. Pass carefully.

facts.text: Avoid driving near collisions if possible, so injured people get help faster.

cites.quote: Avoid driving near collisions, if possible. If anyone is injured, they will get help faster if other vehicles are not blocking the road.

facts.text: If you are in a collision, you must stop.

cites.quote: You must stop. Someone could be injured and need your help.

facts.text: Failing to stop or leaving the scene of a collision is a hit-and-run, and the punishment for conviction is severe.

cites.quote: Failing to stop or leaving the scene of an accident is called a hit-and-run. The punishment is severe if you are convicted of a hit-and-run.

facts.text: If anyone is hurt in a collision, call 911 right away.

cites.quote: Call 911 right away if anyone is hurt.

facts.text: If no one is hurt in a collision, move your vehicle out of traffic and then call 911.

cites.quote: Move your vehicle out of traffic if no one is hurt. Then call 911.

facts.text: After a collision, show your driver's license, vehicle registration card, insurance information, and current address to the other driver, law enforcement, and anyone else involved.

cites.quote: Show your driver’s license, vehicle registration card, insurance information, and current address to the other driver, law enforcement officer, and anyone else involved in the collision.

facts.text: If anyone is injured or killed in a collision, you must report it to law enforcement within 24 hours; your insurance agent, broker, or legal representative can file it for you.

cites.quote: You must make a report to law enforcement within 24 hours of the collision if anyone is injured or killed. Your insurance agent, broker, or legal representative can also file the report.

facts.text: If your vehicle hits or rolls into a parked car or other property, try to find the owner; if you cannot, securely attach a note with your name, phone number, and address and report the collision to law enforcement.

cites.quote: Try to find the owner if your vehicle hits or rolls into a parked car or other property. If you cannot find the owner, leave a note with your name, phone number, and address. Securely attach the note to the vehicle or property. Report the collision to law enforcement.

facts.text: If you kill or injure an animal, call the nearest humane society or law enforcement, and do not try to move an injured animal.

cites.quote: If you kill or injure an animal, call the nearest humane society or law enforcement. Do not try to move an injured animal.

facts.text: You must report a collision to the DMV within 10 days if it caused more than $1,000 in property damage.

cites.quote: If you are in a collision, you must report it to DMV within 10 days if:
The collision caused more than $1,000 in damage to property.

facts.text: You must report a collision to the DMV within 10 days if anyone was injured or killed, even if the injuries were minor.

cites.quote: If you are in a collision, you must report it to DMV within 10 days if:
Anyone was injured or killed. This applies even if the injuries were minor.

facts.text: Each driver must file a Report of Traffic Accident Occurring in California (SR 1) with the DMV, whether or not they caused the collision, even if it happened on private property.

cites.quote: Each driver must file a Report of Traffic Accident Occurring in California (SR 1) with DMV
You (or your representative) must file a report whether or not you caused the collision. This applies even if the collision happened on private property.

facts.text: Your driving privilege will be suspended if you fail to file a required collision report, and law enforcement will not file it for you.

cites.quote: Your driving privilege will be suspended if you fail to file a report. Law enforcement will not make a report for you.

facts.text: A reportable collision is added to your driver's record no matter who caused it.

cites.quote: DMV will add it to your driver’s record. It does not matter who caused the collision.
